scope: Triage across original B01-B71 and new C/F findings including new F12-N1 and C064-N1

roots.reason: One underlying device-token revocation omission: mobile logout does not deactivate prior account's DeviceToken, and server push continues sending to active tokens. F09-N3 and F11-N2 describe the same disclosure from chat previews; C071-N2 traces exact root.

Repeated Stripe base-subscription setup creates recurring provider subscriptions without idempotent guard while local OwnerSubscription tracks a single id. F08-N1 is the invoice-payment variant of B70; B70 also covers extra-seat Checkout. Keep both reproduction scenarios, remediate base and seats as distinct endpoints.
Ethical draft PATCH may have unauthorized destination/product reassignment, and B42 concerns atomicity/error after persistence. Shared endpoint but different vulnerabilities, both retained.

Deleting a shift with bookings and deleting while Stripe Checkout remains open share shift-deletion lifecycle boundary, but need different safety/compensation guards and negative tests. Preserve separate findings.
Roster assignment removal/escalation and generic shift-offer DELETE bypass lifecycle at different entry points. Neither should automatically close the other.
Cancellation penalty paid-once/retry safety is different from overnight negative wage arithmetic; maintain independent test contracts.
Cross-customer invoice.paid subscription entitlement and failure to handle unpaid status both occur in Stripe synchronization but have different causal roots and event cases.
Shift acceptance notification service failure after a committed state and misrouting owner vs posting administrator are distinct delivery/reliability problems.
Mobile chat send error UI missing feedback differs from backend authorization defect allowing revoked chat member to send.
